title: TwinRead
tagline: CONCH and MUSK read every tile like two pathologists; at a 10% review budget the fused reader's own uncertainty catches 80% of its errors (CRC), and a 6 MB int8 student distilled from both runs on an Arduino UNO Q at 18.7 ms per tile.
description:
Pathology already uses a second, independent read for hard cases. **TwinRead** treats the two foundation models the organizers highlight, **CONCH** and **MUSK**, as two independent readers of every H&E tile (linear probes on frozen features). It adds a pre-registered fusion rule, a review flag that decides which tiles go to a pathologist, a census of shared blind spots, two custom CUDA kernels, and an int8 student distilled from both readers, that runs on an offline **Arduino UNO Q** (measured on the board). Model numbers are local-subset numbers (20k NCT-CRC-HE-100K training tiles, full CRC-VAL-HE-7K test; Camelyon17-WILDS unseen hospital 2).

**What the evidence says.** On CRC the fused reader reaches 0.9555 balanced accuracy vs 0.9480 for MUSK (+0.74 pts; tile-level CI, anti-conservative), but large opposing MUS/STR recall swings cancel and the net gain is mostly tumour recall (+3.6 pts); validation chose the rule by 1-2 tiles, and there is no gain on Camelyon17 or for an open-model control pair (PathGen-CLIP + QuiltNet-B-16). On CRC, at a 10% review budget, the fused reader's own uncertainty catches 80.3% of its errors vs 74.1% for MUSK flagging itself; the learned flag that adds disagreement adds nothing, and on Camelyon17 the twin flag does not beat CONCH alone. The honest conclusion: two readers help by giving a better-calibrated fused reader, not because disagreement is informative per se. The pre-registered val-calibrated threshold over-flags CRC test (25.1% for a 10% target) because validation is near ceiling and val → test is a distribution shift.

**Engineering.** K1 turns raw tiles into both readers' inputs in one CUDA launch, bit-exact to the official transforms (90,131 tiles/s with the input on the GPU in the kernel bench). Inside the CONCH + MUSK embedding run it makes preprocessing ×202 faster than PIL, but only ×1.11 end to end because this batched pipeline is GPU-forward-bound. K2 simulates a USB camera filming a screen (SIMULATION) at 46,315 images/s and makes student-training augmentation ×10.6 faster than torch. The 5.65 M-parameter student ties CONCH in fp32 (0.9415); the deployed int8 model (6.0 MB) scores 0.9305 on the board, below every teacher. Its value is being offline, small and cheap.

**Status: partial.** Complete: the OPEN and CM local-subset analyses, both kernels (verified, benchmarked, sanitizer-clean), CM and OPEN students and int8 bundles, the device app and LED sketch running on the UNO Q (18.7 ms per tile at 4 threads, 0.9305 balanced accuracy on all 7,180 CRC test tiles, 25.4 tiles/s for the full loop), the host dashboard (127.0.0.1:1777) and figures. Not done: real camera captures (the board has only seen stored tiles) and the full-data NCSA Delta run (kit in ncsa/). The CONCH/MUSK-derived student is CC-BY-NC-ND and not distributed; the OPEN bundle is the distributable one. Research prototype, not a diagnostic device.
highlights: Fusion (CONCH + MUSK, local subset): CRC-VAL-HE-7K balanced accuracy 0.9555 vs MUSK 0.9480 and CONCH 0.9413 (+0.74 pts, tile-level CI +0.18 to +1.29, anti-conservative). Large opposing MUS/STR recall swings cancel; the net gain is mostly tumour recall (+3.6 pts). No gain on Camelyon17 (−0.40 pts) or for the open control pair (+0.08 pts).

Review flag at a 10% budget (CRC): the fused reader's own uncertainty catches 80.3% of its errors vs 74.1% for MUSK and 66.0% for CONCH flagging themselves; adding disagreement adds nothing (80.3%), and plain disagreement catches 59.0% (it flags the 5.6% disagreements; the rest of the budget is filled in shuffled order). On Camelyon17 the twin flag does not beat CONCH alone.

Pre-registered before any test label (fusion rule, flag, thresholds), out-of-fold student targets, slide-clustered CIs on Camelyon17; reported as measured, including that the val-calibrated threshold over-flags CRC test (25.1% for a 10% target).

K1 CUDA dual preprocess: bit-exact to the official CONCH and MUSK transforms; 90,131 tiles/s with the input on the GPU (46,157 incl. the host copy). In the CONCH + MUSK embedding run, preprocessing is ×202 faster than PIL but end to end only ×1.11, because the model forward is 89.4% of the time.
K2 camera-of-screen augmentation (SIMULATION): 46,315 images/s, ≤ 1 level per op vs a numpy reference, and ×10.6 faster than torch in student training.

Edge student on the Arduino UNO Q, measured on the board: 5.65 M parameters (1.4% of the teachers' vision towers), 6.0 MB int8; 18.7 ms per tile at 4 threads (52.8 ms single-threaded); 0.9305 balanced accuracy on all 7,180 CRC test tiles (OPEN 0.9044), below every teacher; 98.1% of calls match the x86 run. The two device readers are two heads of one student; the board's int8 flag agrees with the teacher flag at kappa 0.32. LED sketch flashed, Bridge RPC verified.
models: wisdomik/QuiltNet-B-16 (reader B, OPEN pair; chosen on validation)
timm mobilenetv4_conv_small (edge student backbone, pretrained trunk)
datasets: 1aurent/NCT-CRC-HE: NCT-CRC-HE-100K 20,007-tile class-balanced subset (17,349 train / 2,658 val, group-disjoint) + full CRC-VAL-HE-7K test (7,180 tiles)
wltjr1007/Camelyon17-WILDS: 7,500-tile subset (train hospitals 0/3/4: 4,500; val hospital 1: 1,500; test hospital 2: 1,500)

images.caption: System overview: CONCH and MUSK read each tile (K1 preprocessing), a fused reader and review signals s1-s4 follow, and a K2-trained int8 student runs on an offline Arduino UNO Q (measured on the board).

Fused vs single readers with 95% CIs. CONCH + MUSK fusion gains +0.74 pts on CRC (tile-level CI, anti-conservative); no gain on Camelyon17 hospital 2 or for the open control pair. Local-subset numbers.

Review flag: errors caught vs review budget. The fused reader's uncertainty (s3) does the work; the learned flag with disagreement (s4) adds nothing; the pre-registered threshold over-flags CRC test. Right: reader errors per class, darkest = the 53 confident shared errors. Bottom: 8 of them (real CRC-VAL-HE-7K tiles).

K1 dual preprocess: bit-exact; 90,131 tiles/s with the input on the GPU (46,157 incl. the host copy); ×202 vs PIL inside the embedding run, ×1.11 end to end (forward-bound). K2 augmentation (simulated camera-of-screen degradation) and its effect on student training. RTX 5060, shared GPU.

Edge student vs teachers on CRC-VAL-HE-7K: fp32 ties CONCH; int8 is below every teacher (int8 costs 2.0 pts for CM, 2.7 for OPEN on x86); 1.4% of the teachers' vision-tower parameters. Board latency and accuracy in the inset.

The int8 student on the Arduino UNO Q, all numbers measured on the board: 18.7 ms per tile at 4 threads, 0.9305 balanced accuracy on all 7,180 CRC test tiles, 25.4 tiles/s for the full loop, 6.0 MB model; LED sketch flashed and Bridge RPC verified on the MCU.

The board runs the int8 student as specified: CM 0.9305 and OPEN 0.9044 on the board match the x86 reference with fused int8 kernels off; the lower committed x86 int8 scores (0.9219, 0.9085) were an onnxruntime kernel artefact.

The device app on the UNO Q (host: Arduino SA,Imola): replay mode on a stored CRC-VAL-HE-7K tile, CM bundle, 53 ms single-threaded latency, LED matrix updated. The bars are two heads of one student, not independent readers. Headless-Chromium screenshot.

hardware: Arduino UNO Q (Qualcomm QRB2210, 4x Cortex-A53 at 2.0 GHz, 3.6 GiB, Debian 13; STM32U585 MCU with the 8x13 LED matrix). Running on the board: the offline device app (replay or camera -> crop + tissue check -> int8 student via onnxruntime -> AGREE/REVIEW with reasons) with a local web UI, and the Bridge-RPC LED-matrix sketch (flashed over USB-C with OpenOCD; set_state verified, 8 ms per call). Measured on the board: 18.7 ms per tile at 4 threads, 0.9305 balanced accuracy on the full CRC test set, 25.4 tiles/s for the full loop. Not done: real camera captures (the board has only seen stored tiles; the screen rig in rig/ is ready).
how_to_run:
cd twinread-conch-musk-edge
bash run_demo.sh --smoke   # no GPU/network: headline JSON, figures, manifest tests, dashboard check
bash run_demo.sh           # data -> OPEN embeddings -> analysis -> student -> bundle -> figures -> dashboard http://127.0.0.1:1777
bash run_demo.sh --with-cm # + CONCH/MUSK local subset (needs HF access)
event_scaleup: Not run. The kit in ncsa/ runs the same pre-registered pipeline on all 100k CRC training tiles with CONCH and MUSK on Delta: J1 (environment, sm_80 kernel build and tests), J2 (embeddings through K1), a CPU analysis job, J3 (student distillation), <= 10 A100-hours. It would show whether the fragile fusion gain holds with 5x the training data. Another reader pair is one PAIRS entry.
limitations: Teacher and student training numbers are local-subset numbers (20k of 100k CRC training tiles; 7.5k Camelyon17 tiles); the full-data Delta run was not done.
CRC has no slide/patient ids: CRC CIs and McNemar tests are tile-level and anti-conservative; validation is group-disjoint, not guaranteed slide-disjoint.

The CRC fusion gain is fragile: large opposing MUS/STR recall swings cancel and the net gain is mostly tumour recall; the rule was chosen by 1-2 validation tiles; no gain on Camelyon17 or for the open pair.

The review flag's value comes from the fused reader's uncertainty, not disagreement; the pre-registered val-calibrated threshold over-flags CRC test, and on Camelyon17 the twin flag does not beat CONCH alone.
Confident shared errors (0.74% of CRC tiles) cannot be caught by any two-reader disagreement signal.
The int8 student is below every teacher on test; the device's two 'readers' are two heads on one shared backbone, and the board's int8 flag agrees with the teacher flag only at kappa 0.32.
The board has only run on stored tiles (replay); there are no real camera captures, and camera robustness numbers are the K2 simulation.
Kernel throughput is measured on a shared GPU (estimate); sm_80/sm_90 builds are compile-checked only.
The CONCH/MUSK-derived student is CC-BY-NC-ND and not distributed; only the OPEN bundle is distributable.
Research prototype, not a diagnostic device; no clinical validation.

metrics.uno_q_latency: 18.7 ms p50 per tile (int8 CM student, 4 threads, measured on the board)

lay.what: TwinRead lets two AI models look at the same small patch of a tissue slide. It works like two doctors giving separate opinions. It combines their answers and marks patches a pathologist should check again. A small copy runs on a cheap offline computer board in about 19 ms per patch.
lay.why: Second opinions catch mistakes, but they cost a second expert's time. If software can point to the uncertain patches, a pathologist can spend review time where it matters. A small offline version could someday help clinics without slide scanners, powerful computers or reliable internet.
lay.impressive: When only one in ten tissue patches is sent to a pathologist, the combined model's own doubt catches 80.3% of its mistakes on a public colon tissue test set of 7,180 patches. The better single model, checking itself the same way, catches 74.1%.
